pages.text: A still with a reflux column: vapour rises, condenses, and runs back down over what is rising, again and again. Each pass enriches it; the purity grows as 1 − e^(−0.6R) with the reflux ratio R. The still must run above the stage's boiling point, and the more of the condensate is sent back, the slower the product comes off.
$(thing)Set$(): Still temperature, Reflux ratio.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Draughts: the column's efficiency varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): It boils over.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Hotter is faster; more reflux is slower.
